comment: Task set VERSION 2 for the reconstruction bench. v1 (reconstruction_bench_tasks.json, frozen 2026-07-28, sha256 5c74f55f402b461df2afc2ecf2e2c629b82004b9134839e44db32330c9534e41) is UNCHANGED and remains the frozen instrument for any replay of the 2026-07-28 and 2026-08-20-wave-1 runs; v2 does not supersede its bundles. What changed: every DATED LIVE-STATE must-atom is replaced by a STRUCTURAL one - the task names a resolver, the resolver reads the live store at score time and returns the atoms. An atom entry is a literal string (must appear), a list (any-of: one member must appear), or {"resolve": "<resolver>", "arg": ...} which expands to either of those. Resolvers live in scripts/reconstruction_bench_resolvers.py and are pure functions of the tree.
resolution_rule: A task's atoms resolve from the node the wake names as that shard's `source`. The bench therefore measures TRANSMISSION - does the payload at rate R still carry what its own source says - not store freshness. Resolving a rendered shard's atoms from a row store the render has not caught up with would score staleness as a rate failure, which is a different experiment.
scoring: unchanged from v1: the shared normalizer + must-atom matcher in scripts/reconstruction_bench.py (normalize/score), identical for every arm and every answer.
shard_axis: Every task declares the payload `shard` (or block) that carries its answer, so a run can report which shard each failure indicts. Blocks marked rate_invariant are OUTSIDE lever 2's reach by construction (probe, semantic, identity, triple) - they are declared positive controls, not ladder rungs.

Atoms resolve LIVE from the render's row-sources (HANDOFF.md's 'Full record' line; OPEN_STACK.md's first live fork id) so the dynamic block re-anchors every close - the triple is a render whose sources move, unlike T19-T21's static source strings. rate_invariant on the same structural ground as T19-T21: triple is a top-level fixed_point key outside the shards list lever 2 walks.

tasks.question: The 2026-08-20 audit-day amendment banks a cluster of rulings rather than a sentence. What are its first two rulings, and under which PV stamps were they banked?
tasks.structural_note: Minted 2026-08-23 (WO-20260821-law-atom-past-the-prefix). THE INSTRUMENT GAP IT CLOSES: T04/T05/T06 all resolve through `_clause`, whose atom is the amendment's first sentence capped at 110, and `self_corpus.law_digest` cuts the same tail at `_LAW_CLAUSE_CAP`. Every cap at or above 110 therefore carries those atoms whole, so the standing-law class scored 3/3 at 110, 120, 130 and 160 alike and could not say whether a shorter digest was still usable law (RES-20260820-minimum-law-digest, evidence/WAKE_RATE_BENCH_2026-08-20/law_digest_bisection/). T23 resolves through `law.amendment_rulings`, which ends the span on a RULING boundary instead of a character count: the audit-day amendment is a `·`-separated cluster with no sentence end anywhere in 958 chars, so its clause is truncated at the cap at every rung including the incumbent, and its span through the second ruling is 135 chars - 25 clear of the scorer's 110 needle, 25 clear of the incumbent 160. Measured break (evidence/LAW_ATOM_PAST_THE_PREFIX_2026-08-23/): PASS at cap 160/140/136/135, FAIL at 134/130/120/110, at both the A0 and the shipping-budget arm - the class reads 4/4 above the break and 3/4 below it where it used to read 3/3 at every one of them. The length is a property of the law's wording, not of any cap, and the atom is not clamped to the digest - if an amendment is re-worded past the cap the task goes red, which is the reading the instrument owes. `_amendment_by_slug` now searches the bolded-inclusive amendment list so the cluster bullets are addressable; `law.latest_*` still reads the plain-dated series, and all 22 pre-existing tasks resolve to byte-identical atoms (checked before and after). rate_invariant on the same ground as T04-T06: identity is outside _BUDGET_SACRIFICE_RANK.
